g: proporcionen a sus esclavos
An affirmative ustedes command; a introduces the people receiving what is provided.
e: un Amo en el cielo
The capitalized Amo creates a contrast with the human masters directly addressed.

g: perseveren en ella
perseveren is a ustedes command; ella refers back to the feminine noun oración.
e: con agradecimiento
con introduces the attitude accompanying persevering in prayer.

g: a fin de que Dios nos abra
a fin de que expresses purpose and takes subjunctive abra; nos is indirect object.
e: las puertas para proclamar
A metaphor of opened doors for opportunity; para introduces what the doors permit.

g: Oren para que yo lo anuncie
Oren is a command; para que takes subjunctive anuncie, and lo refers to the mystery.
e: como debo hacerlo
como means ‘as’; debo + infinitive expresses obligation, with lo for the message.

g: Compórtense sabiamente
An affirmative ustedes command; sabiamente is an adverb describing how they should behave.
e: al máximo cada momento oportuno
al máximo means ‘to the fullest’; oportuno describes the available moment.

g: Que su conversación sea
Que + subjunctive sea forms an exhortation; su conversación is its singular subject.
e: de buen gusto
An idiom for being tasteful or appropriate; it characterizes conversation.

g: les contará en detalle
les is indirect object; contará is future, ‘will tell you in detail’.
e: fiel servidor y colaborador
Two masculine nouns coordinated by y describe Tíquico’s service.

g: para que tengan noticias
para que requires subjunctive tengan and gives the purpose of sending him.
e: cobren ánimo
cobrar ánimo is an idiom meaning ‘take heart’ or ‘be encouraged’.

g: que es uno de ustedes
que refers to Onésimo; es is singular and uno agrees with the male referent.
e: los pondrán al tanto
poner al tanto means ‘bring up to date’; los is the group being informed.

g: si va a visitarlos, recíbanlo
si + present va a visitarlos gives a possible case; recíbanlo is the resulting command.
e: mi compañero de cárcel
de cárcel identifies Aristarco as a companion in imprisonment.

g: me han sido de mucho consuelo
me is indirect object; han sido is present perfect and de consuelo states their effect.
e: en pro del reino de Dios
en pro de is a formal phrase meaning ‘for the benefit of’ or ‘in support of’.

g: para que ... se mantengan firmes
para que introduces purpose and takes subjunctive se mantengan.
e: luchando en oración
luchar en oración depicts sustained effort expressed through prayer.

g: A mí me consta que
A mí and me are an emphatic indirect-object doubling: ‘I know for certain that’.
e: se preocupa mucho por ustedes
preocuparse por means ‘be concerned about’; mucho intensifies the concern.

g: Los saludan Lucas ... y Demas
The verb precedes its plural compound subject, Lucas and Demas.
e: el querido médico
querido is an affectionate adjective agreeing with the masculine noun médico.

g: la iglesia que se reúne
que begins a relative clause modifying iglesia; se reúne is singular reflexive.
e: en su casa
su may mean his, her, their, or your; here the context identifies Ninfas’s house.

g: Una vez que se les haya leído
Una vez que takes present perfect subjunctive haya leído for a future completed event.
e: la carta dirigida a esa iglesia
dirigida agrees with carta and a identifies the intended recipient.

g: Díganle a Arquipo que se ocupe
Díganle is a plural command with le; que se ocupe is subjunctive after telling.
e: que la lleve a cabo
llevar a cabo is an idiom meaning ‘carry out’ or ‘complete’; la refers to tarea.

g: Que la gracia sea con ustedes
Que + subjunctive sea creates the letter’s closing blessing.
e: de mi puño y letra
An idiom meaning ‘in my own handwriting’, emphasizing Paul’s personal hand.
